parts.label: (a)
parts.stem:
Chloric(I) acid, $\text{HClO}$, is a weak Brønsted-Lowry acid.

When chloric(I) acid is added to aqueous sodium hydroxide, an acid-base reaction takes place, as shown.

$$\text{HClO} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{NaClO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Identify the **two** conjugate acid-base pairs in this reaction.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
The value for the acid dissociation constant, $K_{\text{a}}$, of $\text{HClO(aq)}$ is $3.70 \times 10^{-8}$.

Calculate the concentration, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, of $\text{HClO(aq)}$ at a pH of 4.51.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
When a solution of $\text{HClO(aq)}$ is heated, chloric(V) acid and a strong acid **not** containing oxygen are formed as the only products.

Write an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Suggest a substance that could be added to aqueous ethanoic acid to form a buffer solution.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Some fertilisers contain calcium dihydrogenphosphate, $\text{Ca}(\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4)_2$.

An aqueous solution containing dihydrogenphosphate ions, $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$, can act as a buffer solution.

Write **two** equations to show how $\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^-$ ions can act as a buffer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The solubility of calcium phosphate, $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2$, is $1.14 \times 10^{-7} \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ at $25^{\circ}\text{C}$.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
The expression for the solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2$ is shown.

$$K_{\text{sp}} = [\text{Ca}^{2+}]^3[\text{PO}_4^{3-}]^2$$

Calculate the value of $K_{\text{sp}}$ for $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2$. Include units.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
Some solid sodium phosphate is added to a saturated solution of $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2$.

Predict the effect, if any, on the solubility of $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2$.

Explain your answer.
